chunks: My father narrated, may God be pleased with him, said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Yaqoob ibn Yazid, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, who linked it up to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).
He said: Whoever patches his collar like this, mends his shoes, and carries his merchandise, has been saved from haughtiness.

key_terms.جَيْبَهُ: his collar or neck opening of a garment

ai.seo_question: What practical actions does the Imam recommend to avoid arrogance and haughtiness?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights these specific, humble acts—patching one's own collar, mending one's shoes, and carrying one's goods—as tangible safeguards against *kibr* (haughtiness), emphasizing that true nobility lies in self-sufficiency rather than status. This tradition underscores the Shia ethical principle that physical humility in daily chores cultivates spiritual modesty, preventing the soul from becoming inflated by worldly pride.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-78 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted on the authority of Yaqoob ibn Yazid, on the authority of Abdul Rahman ibn Abi Najran who linked it up through a chain of narrators to Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB), “
Whoever patches up his collar, mends his shoes and carries his merchandise will be saved from haughtiness.”
